question: Human rights and the rule of law in Tanzania have been in a state of steady, serious decline, culminating in the systemic repression of opposition parties, human rights defenders and civil society.

On 6 November, the High Court of Tanzania convicted Tundu Lissu – leader of Tanzania’s main opposition party, Chama Cha Demokrasia Na Maendeleo (CHADEMA, Party for Democracy and Progress) – of incitement, sentencing him to four years in prison. According to CHAMEDA, 51 party officials were arrested and accused of terrorism after the government outlawed all political gatherings in view of youth-led protests.
The legal proceedings have sparked major human rights concerns, as Lissu defended himself after saying that the authorities had denied him private access to legal counsel.

In light of the above, can the Commission say how it intends to make political dialogue, development cooperation and financial aid programmes with the Tanzanian Government subject to and conditional on tangible and verifiable commitments to uphold the rule of law, fundamental freedoms and the international human rights treaties binding on the country?
